newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr creeps up by late Tokyo on weak euro concerns.
newsitem.headline: Dlr creeps up by late Tokyo on weak euro concerns.

text.p: 0630 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar edged up against the yen and the mark by late Tokyo trade due to short-covering amid lingering uncertainty over the European single currency.

Corrective mark buying against the dollar took place earlier in the day, but the mark retreated by late trade as traders remained preoccupied with concerns about a weak euro and a row between the Bonn government and the Bundesbank.

"What has been happening is selling of the German mark in favour of the dollar or the Japanese yen," said a senior trader at a Japanese bank. Traders in Tokyo were focusing on remarks by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel at 0700 GMT over the revaluation of the Bundesbank's gold assets.

Waigel said on Tuesday he had reached a "good compromise" with Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer under which the transfer of gold profits to government coffers would be postponed until 1998. But he said later in the day that no deal had been reached and that talks to resolve the contentious gold debate would continue.
Traders said earlier mark buying did not have a lasting impact in pushing the dollar lower as traders saw the revaluation plan having been watered down but not abolished.
"There is a possibility of further mark sales later in Europe, depending on comments by Waigel," said one trader.

The dollar has strengthened against the mark as a broader euro and looser criteria for entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU) is regarded as a more likely scenerio than a delay in the EMU start date, dealers said.
A postponement of EMU could spark a strong wave of buying back of the mark, they added.

The dollar's strength against the mark has also helped lift the dollar against the yen, although its rise against the Japanese currency has been slow due to persistent selling pressure by Japanese exporters and hedge sales by investors.
Meanwhile, the downside was solid due to talk of bids at around 115.80 yen by trust banks related to fresh foreign investment by pension funds, said a dealer at a European bank.
Banking sources said about 300 billion yen in fresh pension money was likely to be invested via trust banks in foreign assets, such as stocks and bonds, by the middle of this month.

Separately, there was also speculation that public fund bodies may invest in foreign assets, using money earned from redemption of Japanese government bonds, dealers said. About five trillion yen of government bonds will mature on June 20.
Singapore dealers said activity was sluggish in the dollar/majors, largely due to a lack of fresh incentives.

"For the mark/yen, if the mark breaks 67.50 yen, it might go higher. If not, it'll stay stuck between 67.10 and 67.40," said a dealer in Singapore. Tokyo dealers said stop-loss mark sales could emerge if it falls below 67 yen.---Singapore newsroom (65-8703080)---Tatsuo Ito in Tokyo 81-3-3432-1396
